metadataReview.note: Regesta Imperii records the battle of 9 June 1075 “bei Homburg an der Unstrut”: the royal army of Henry IV, having advanced to Behringen near the Saxon camp, attacked the surprised Saxons, many of whom drowned in the Unstrut during their flight. The atlas point marks the vanished Homburg castle and monastery site south of Thamsbrück as a sector reference only. German Wikipedia also records the alternative name “Schlacht bei Hohenburg und Nägelstedt”, so the precise battlefield is not fixed. The existing date is retained. Strengths, losses and equipment are not inferred.

metadataReview.coordinateBasis: OpenStreetMap node 2146023970 (historic=archaeological_site, archaeological_site=fortification, name Homburg, linked to Wikidata Q1625884) is at latitude 51.1298387, longitude 10.6339308, rounded to [10.6339,51.1298]. Alle Burgen places the vanished Burg Homburg about 1,000 m south of Thamsbrück on the steep slope above the Unstrut floodplain, with a later monastery on the same site; the OSM point lies about 1.1 km south of the Thamsbrück village node. Regesta Imperii identifies the battle’s “Hoenburg” with this completely vanished castle on the Unstrut near Langensalza. The point is the eponymous castle-site reference, not the Saxon camp, the royal approach from Behringen or the Unstrut where fleeing Saxons drowned. The battlefield extent is not established and no accuracy radius is claimed.
